title: DO NOT USE!!!!!!!!
text: I spent approximately seven months working with a freelancer on an app development project through Fiverr. Throughout that time, I repeatedly reported major issues, participated in multiple Zoom meetings, and provided screenshots, videos, and detailed feedback. I continued giving opportunities to fix the project because Fiverr Support encouraged me to do so. When I ultimately requested a refund because the application was still not in a usable, production-ready state, Fiverr focused almost entirely on the age of the order and its cancellation policy rather than the overall history of the project. My request to escalate the case was not meaningfully addressed, and I was repeatedly told the order was “too old” to cancel. As a customer, I expected Fiverr to evaluate whether the service I paid for was actually delivered as agreed, not simply rely on procedural deadlines. My experience left me feeling that customer protection becomes very limited once enough time has passed, even if you’ve spent months trying to resolve issues in good faith. Based on my experience, I would encourage anyone using Fiverr for large, long-term software development projects to carefully understand the platform’s policies before investing significant time and money.

text: I’ve had this app installed for a while. I’m trying to add images to an existing layout. I can’t drag them around to rearrange, or add images to existing placeholders. The AI help bot says it’s a bug. A pretty big bug, I’d say. So far my experience has been that this app is worthless. UPDATE: I contacted support via email. There’s no way to save a session to continue it later. The Export function lets you export a jpeg or a png of the screen with a “Share” button, but the “Save” button apparently does nothing. I tried searching for a solution, and came up empty. Somehow I discovered that the Smartist app saves the jpeg into the User Library/Containers folder with a long code name. No dialog to select the folder; no way to change its name. The bot couldn’t help me with that; and an email to the “help” desk was never responded to. The biggest failure of this app is the lack of any clear documentation. Its quirky user interface and lack of features that have been with Mac for years lead me to recommend other ways of modeling artwork in a physical environment. This app has promise, and some of the customization features are interesting, like the ability to remove or add other objects seem like they’d be useful. text: I signed up for this app based on a wave of glowing reviews, but it’s hard to ignore the suspicion that many of these are incentivized—likely written by affiliates or paid reviewers. The actual product is far from what’s advertised. Functionally, the app is deeply flawed. Its design engine doesn’t enable meaningful creation; instead, it relies on a rudimentary algorithm that randomly pulls images from online sources and attempts to fit them into predefined spaces. There’s no real customization, no intelligent layout logic, and certainly no design intuition. It feels more like a collage generator than a professional design tool. Customer service is equally disappointing. I requested a refund shortly after realizing the app’s limitations, but received no response whatsoever. No acknowledgment, no follow-up—just silence. This app is not ready for serious use. It may one day evolve into something useful, but in its current state, it’s a waste of time and money. I strongly advise others to look elsewhere for reliable design solutions.
